newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai army chief urges non-intervention precedent.
newsitem.headline: Thai army chief urges non-intervention precedent.

text.p: Thailand's army commander in chief General Pramon Phalasin said on Thursday the military should set a precedent by not intervening in the country's current political wrangling.

"I would like to urge all the soldiers to distance themselves from the ongoing chaos and let politicians settle their own problems in order to set a precedent and show that the democratic system can progress without intervention," Pramon told reporters.
"With this precedent we can prevent power-hungry people from using political choas as an excuse to drag in the armed forces," Pramon said.

Members of the governing six-party coalition are engaged in a fierce tussle to decide on a successor to Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa, who said on Saturday he would step down from his post in seven days.
Pramon was speaking after reports that Defence Minister General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh was holding an urgent meeting with the chief of the armed forces.
In the past the military has been accused of taking advantage of party infighting and political uncertainty to topple governments.
Thailand has had 17 attempted or successful coups since parliamentary democracy replaced an absolute monarchy in 1932.
Pramon also urged politicians to set aside individual ambitions and desire for personal gain and find the acceptable person to replace Banharn.

"It is not difficult to find a qualified person to be the next prime minister, provided that the politicians set aside individual ambitions and thoughts of personal gain. One must take the national interest as the priority," Pramon said.
The coalition partners have not yet been able to agree on a successor.

Chavalit, who leads the second largest coalition party, is seen as the front runner, while many in Banharn's Chart Thai party support party elder Pramarn Adireksarn. Nam Thai leader and foreign minister Amnuay Viravan is a compromise choice.
Former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, leader of the opposition Chart Pattana party, is also seen to be in the running for Thailand's top job.
Chatichai was ousted in February 1991 in Thailand's last coup when the military overthrew his elected government in a bloodless putsch.
